title: Pinch Valve

introduction.definition: A pinch valve controls flow by squeezing a flexible elastomer sleeve. Open, it is a straight full-bore tube; closed, the sleeve is pinched shut. Only the sleeve touches the fluid, so it handles abrasive slurries, powders and corrosive liquids without pockets or crevices.
applications: Mineral and alumina slurries (red mud, lime, tailings)
key_points: Sleeve is the only wear part
Pressure and temperature limited by the elastomer
introduction.summary: A pinch valve closes by squeezing a flexible elastomer sleeve. The liquid touches only the sleeve, and the open valve is a straight, full-bore tube, so pinch valves handle abrasive slurries, powders and corrosive liquids with no pockets to clog.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Near-linear to equal-percentage throttling over the middle of the stroke; avoid long throttling at very small openings (wear).

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Flush the line before installing the valve so welding debris cannot damage seats.
Provide isolation and drain/vent points for maintenance.
Allow access for the handwheel/actuator and for removal of internals.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

routine.task: Check for sleeve leakage at the housing drain.

periodic.task: Replace sleeve on schedule or at first sign of cracking.

overhaul.task: Check pinch bars and stem threads.

lubrication: Lubricate stem threads and operator gearing per the manufacturer; most wetted internals need no lubrication.

video_tutorials.title: Pinch Valve — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Pinch Valve.
A pinch valve controls flow by squeezing a flexible elastomer sleeve.
Open, it is a straight full-bore tube; closed, the sleeve is pinched shut.
Only the sleeve touches the fluid, so it handles abrasive slurries, powders and corrosive liquids without pockets or crevices.
Typical applications include mineral and alumina slurries (red mud, lime, tailings); cement, sand and powder conveying; wastewater sludge; chemical and food dosing.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Valve Housing with Flanges & Yoke.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Pinch Valve works.
Open: slurry passes straight through the full-bore sleeve.
Turning the handwheel drives the upper pinch bar down.
Links pull the lower bar up at the same time (double pinch).
The sleeve flattens and seals across the bore.
The housing contains the sleeve and supports the mechanism.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Pinch Valve — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Pinch Valve.
Check for sleeve leakage at the housing drain.
Replace sleeve on schedule or at first sign of cracking.
Check pinch bars and stem threads.
Watch for sleeve rupture: leak from housing. Common cause: fatigue, abrasion, over-closing.
Watch for incomplete closure: passing. Common cause: solids trapped, worn sleeve.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
